title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 73
paragraphs: These men, having thus been placed in bonds, were put to death; and the Athenians after this sent for Cleisthenes to return, and also for the seven hundred families that had been driven out by Cleomenes. They then sent envoys to Sardis, desiring to make an alliance with the Persians, for they were well aware that the Lacedaemonians and Cleomenes had been made their utter enemies. When these envoys reached Sardis and were saying what they had been instructed to say, Artaphrenes son of Hystaspes, governor of Sardis, asked who these men were who were requesting to be allies of the Persians, and where on earth they lived; and having heard this from the envoys, he summed up his answer to them thus: that if the Athenians were willing to give earth and water to Darius, he was willing to make alliance with them, but if not, he bade them begone. The envoys, taking it upon themselves, said that they were willing to do so, because they desired to make the alliance.
